name: GitHub
tagline: GitHub App access, sign-in, and event triggers
description: Install your installation's GitHub App on the repositories you choose. Agents clone, branch and push with the App's installation token, open pull requests when asked, and GitHub events can start work.
seoTitle: GitHub Integration for AI Coding Agents | SAM
seoDescription: Connect GitHub repositories to SAM through a GitHub App. Agents push branches and open pull requests, and issues, comments, pull requests and pushes can start agent work.

features.title: GitHub App access
features.description: You choose which repositories the App can reach. Agents use its installation token, not your personal token.

features.title: Pull requests when asked
features.description: Agents work on their own branches, push them when a task is done, and open a pull request when you ask.

features.title: Event triggers
features.description: An issue, issue comment, pull request or push that matches your filters can start an agent with a saved profile.

features.title: Sign in with GitHub
features.description: One of the sign-in options your installation can offer, alongside Google, GitLab and email codes.

howItWorks.description: The self-hosting guide's wizard creates your installation's own GitHub App with its settings filled in.
Install the App on an organization or account and pick the repositories it can access.
Choose a repository when you create a SAM project.
Agents clone, branch, commit and push with the App's token.

useCases.title: Issue triage
useCases.description: Start an agent for each new issue with a given label and have it investigate.

useCases.title: Comment commands
useCases.description: Let teammates trigger an agent from a pull request or issue comment.

useCases.title: Several repositories
useCases.description: One project per repository, with agents running across all of them.

faq.question: Which permissions does the App need?
faq.answer: Contents read and write, plus read-only metadata, email, pull requests, checks, actions and issues. Grant pull requests read and write only if agents should open pull requests. The self-hosting guide walks through it.

faq.question: Do agents use my GitHub token?
faq.answer: No. Repository operations use the GitHub App installation token. Your personal sign-in is used to sign you in to SAM.

faq.question: Does SAM support GitHub Enterprise Server?
faq.answer: No. SAM supports GitHub.com. For a self-managed Git server, GitLab with a custom host is supported.

name: GitLab
tagline: GitLab.com or your own GitLab server
description: Back a project with a GitLab repository. SAM uses the project owner's GitLab sign-in to clone and push, and your administrator can point SAM at GitLab.com or a self-managed GitLab host.
seoTitle: GitLab Integration for AI Coding Agents | SAM
seoDescription: Run SAM coding agents against GitLab repositories on GitLab.com or a self-managed GitLab server. Agents push branches you can turn into merge requests.

features.title: GitLab.com or self-managed
features.description: The administrator sets the GitLab host, client ID and secret in Admin → Integrations.

features.title: Sign in with GitLab
features.description: Users can sign in to SAM with GitLab when the administrator enables it.

features.title: Branches, not surprises
features.description: On a GitLab project the agent pushes its branch, and you open the merge request in GitLab.

howItWorks.description: The administrator registers an OAuth application in GitLab and enters it in Admin → Integrations.
Sign in with GitLab so SAM can reach your repositories.
Pick a GitLab repository when you create the project.

useCases.title: Self-managed Git
useCases.description: Keep source on your own GitLab server while agents run on your own cloud.

useCases.title: Mixed teams
useCases.description: Run GitHub-backed and GitLab-backed projects in the same installation.

faq.question: Whose access does SAM use?
faq.answer: The project owner's GitLab sign-in, which reaches the projects that account can reach.

faq.question: Can agents open merge requests?
faq.answer: Not yet. Agents push a branch, and you open the merge request in GitLab.

faq.question: Do GitHub event triggers work for GitLab?
faq.answer: No. Use a webhook trigger from GitLab instead.

name: Cloudflare Workers AI
tagline: Built-in models for SAM features and for your agents
description: Workers AI comes with the Cloudflare account that runs SAM. SAM uses it for task titles, text to speech, voice input and the SAM assistant, and agents can call its models while they work within a monthly budget.
seoTitle: Built-in AI with Cloudflare Workers AI | SAM
seoDescription: SAM uses Cloudflare Workers AI for task titles, text to speech, voice input and the SAM assistant, and lets agents call Workers AI models within a monthly budget.

features.title: No separate model key
features.description: Workers AI is billed to the Cloudflare account that runs your SAM installation.

features.title: Models for your agents
features.description: Agents can call Workers AI models, such as a yes-or-no decision model or Whisper for transcription, within a monthly budget per project.

features.title: Platform features
features.description: Task titles, reading messages aloud, voice input and the SAM assistant use Workers AI models.

features.title: AI Gateway where it fits
features.description: Task titles and the AI proxy go through Cloudflare AI Gateway for logging and limits. Speech and transcription call the model directly.

howItWorks.description: Workers AI is bound to the SAM Worker when you deploy. There is nothing to connect.
Give agents a monthly budget for Workers AI calls in project settings.
Administrators see AI usage and cost on the admin pages.

useCases.title: Small decisions inside a task
useCases.description: Let an agent ask a cheap model a yes-or-no question instead of spending its main model's tokens.

useCases.title: Speech in and out
useCases.description: Dictate prompts and have replies read aloud.

faq.question: Does Workers AI need its own API key?
faq.answer: No. It uses the Cloudflare account that runs SAM. Self-hosting SAM needs the Workers Paid plan.

faq.question: Can my coding agent use Workers AI as its main model?
faq.answer: Not directly. Coding agents use their own providers. Agents can call Workers AI models as a tool alongside their main model.

faq.question: Which models does SAM use?
faq.answer: Gemma 4 26B for task titles and preparing text for speech, Deepgram Aura 2 for text to speech and Whisper for voice input. The SAM assistant and AI proxy models are set per installation.
